newsitem.title: USA: UN arms head says Iraq's Aziz offers cooperation.
newsitem.headline: UN arms head says Iraq's Aziz offers cooperation.

text.p: Incoming U.N. chief arms inspector Richard Butler said Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz offered to cooperate fully with U.N. weapons inspectors Wednesday.

Butler characterized his first meeting with Aziz as productive, but refused to say whether he discussed recent Iraqi blocks on UN inspections which led the U.N. Security Council this past weekend to sternly warn Baghdad to comply with future inspection requests or face further sanctions.
"The deputy prime minister indicated to me that he would be happy to work with me and offered full cooperation.
"So, that was a good way to start and I'm very satisified. I would probably say that this is a meeting that demonstrated a new and renewed sense of purpose," Butler said.
Baghdad had claimed that UN inspectors were violating Iraqi sovereignty by seeking to examine sensitive intelligence sites and claimed inspectors entered religious holy sites.

Butler, an Australian diplomat, will assume control of the UN's Special Commission on Iraq (UNSCOM) on July 1, replacing Rolf Ekeus, who is departing to Washington to serve as Sweden's ambassodor to the United States.
"The deputy prime minister gave me a history of Iraq's involvement with UNSCOM, to which I listened attentively," Butler said.

"I replied by saying I thought the job was one that should be marked by objectivity and I intend to pursue it that way, including, as far as possible, avoiding any political statements because that's not my job.
"My job is to work with Iraq, trying to find and eliminate the problem of weapons of mass destruction."
Aziz arrived in New York to attend the Earth Summit at the U.N.
The U.N.'s regular 60-day review of the sanctions against Iraq was cancelled as part of last weekend's Security Council reprimand.
((-- Pat Connole, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620))
